persona: Apparel art director for independent labels

designs.title: Barley and Malt
designs.why: Real engraved-plate feel: clean solid line hatching that will screen well on both tees, good serif typography, a story (grain to malt) a brewery-adjacent customer gets. Composition is tidy but a bit textbook-even; the four-stage row reads small from 3 m.
designs.fix: Enlarge the barley ear to own the top two-thirds as the hero and tighten the malting row into a single band so there is a clear focal point instead of an even grid.

designs.title: Vitis vinifera
designs.why: Lovely subject and leaf drawing, but the grapes, cane and bottle are rendered as a fine stochastic dither; at 300 DPI those dots will plug or drop out on cotton and look muddy. The generic labelled wine bottle and glass also drag it from botanical plate toward wine-shop clip art.
designs.fix: Re-render the tones as engraved line hatching (no dither dots), and replace the bottle/glass with a second botanical element such as a leaf underside or flower cluster.

designs.title: Fermentation
designs.why: Good idea and the vessel line work is crisp, but up close the krausen and bubble fill is garbled squiggles and question-mark-like glyphs, and the graph/phase-table half reads like a homework diagram rather than a graphic. It loses the lab-poster charm at $50.
designs.fix: Redraw the tank interior with deliberate, clean bubble circles and stipple, and cut the line graph so the cutaway tank plus the magnified yeast become the composition.

designs.title: Oak Barrel
designs.why: The strongest blueprint here: crisp single-weight technical line, real dimensions, exploded staves and hoop details make a credible cooper's sheet that looks great white-on-black. Clean vectors that will print sharp; type is legible at full size.
designs.fix: Bump the stroke weight of the hoop and dimension lines slightly (thin lines approach the limit for a one-colour screen on black) and give the elevation drawing more scale as the hero.

designs.title: Pot Still
designs.why: Strong silhouette and a satisfying copper-still cutaway with old-engraving character; reads well from distance. Heavy solid areas and cross-hatch dither in the fire and brick zones are dense and will print heavy and stiff on the white tee.
designs.fix: Open up the darkest zones (firebox, worm tub interior) by thinning hatching and replacing the cross-hatch dither with line hatching to cut ink coverage and keep the print soft.

designs.title: Joiner's Tools
designs.why: Charming vintage catalogue page with clean engraved tools and convincing No./size labelling; the kind of graphic an indie workwear label actually sells. Line quality holds up at full size and will screen cleanly.
designs.fix: Fill the slight dead space at bottom left and tighten the layout so the plane, chisels and saw sit on a stronger grid with a small catalogue header to frame it.

designs.title: Shaping
designs.why: Evocative scene with a strong label word, but it is a photo-like illustration converted to fine dither: up close the face, respirator and hands dissolve into noise, and the whole thing will print as a grey smudge with dot gain. Highest ink load of the set and a rectangular, unvignetted feel.
designs.fix: Redraw as true line engraving with solid blacks and clean hatching (no dither), and vignette the scene so it does not sit as a hard-edged block on the back.

designs.title: Motorcycle
designs.why: Workshop-manual concept is very sellable and the layout with detail views and spec table is right, but the line work is wobbly and broken in places (engine casing, brake section) with blobby artefacts that read as auto-traced. Looks cheap next to the barrel sheet.
designs.fix: Clean up and redraw the bike and engine line work with consistent stroke weight and closed shapes, keeping the existing layout and spec table.
